turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I've been having just a worsening breathlessness. I've been also having a cough, and I think I might have also had a fever in the last couple weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um so the breathlessness started six weeks ago, correct?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and then when did the cough start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'd say around the same time the breathlessness started, so around six weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And then the fever?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The fever I've kind of had on and off in the last couple weeks. I would say two to three weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK um and do you, how often are you having this breathlessness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I would say it's pretty much there most of the time. It sometimes gets worse when I'm exerting myself, but I think just baseline, I feel like I've been able to breathe less heavily than before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so alright, and how long does it last when you do get it? Or is it just always there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it's kind of just there, but then when it's getting worse like it lasts a couple minutes to, I would say like 10 to 15 minutes and then it goes back to like just the normal breathlessness.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and if you were to describe the quality of your breathlessness, would you say that it feels like a kind of like a burning feeling, like you're having a hard time catching your breath or does it feel like you're breathing too fast?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think it's more I just can't seem to take like deep breaths. And then when I get breathless, I I really try to take a deep breath but I just can't find myself catching my breath at that time. So it's just more not being able to catch my breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sure. And are there things that make make it better or worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, not really, I think it's sometimes moving around too much, but like nothing, nothing really causes it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, and was there any sort of trigger six weeks ago that you think may have like caused all of your symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh I'm not sure I I don't think there was any triggers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, has anyone around you been sick?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So there there are some people living in my house that have a bad cough over the last few weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So they have similar symptoms to you as well then?

turns.text: Yeah, some of them like don't really have the shortness of breath and it's just like a cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But yeah, there are some of them also have some shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK. And have you traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I actually came to Canada one year ago. I'm originally from India and I I'm I came here to study.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, um alright. If you were to rate your breathlessness from one to 10, 10 being the worst, how bad is your breathlessness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It can get pretty bad. Like I I would say up to an 8 sometimes, maybe a couple times a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you ever experienced this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, this is like the first time I'm having this issue.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you feel like it's getting worse, better, has it changed since you started having these symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think it's getting worse and that's why I was getting a bit scared and I came here.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Yeah, that was a good call and have you had any changes to your smell recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no changes to smell.

turns.text: Uh, no, not really, no.

turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, and the coughing, are you coughing up any blood?

turns.text: Uh, I don't think so. Sometimes, like when I cough up like sputum, there is like a little bit of pink, pink tinged sputum as well. Sometimes it's like brownish in color and sometimes it's green, but I haven't actually coughed up any blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and you said there's some sputum like pink tinged sputum. How much sputum would you say you cough up every time you cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No OK, how about cancers?

turns.text: OK OK, so you mentioned you moved to Canada from India about a year back. Where do you live now?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, for sure. So the first thing we want to rule out is TB. So, we can do like a AFB smear or I think they have other diagnostic work up for that too. So we'll do that first. If not, we can check to see if it's like another, another typical pneumonia, we can do a chest X Ray for that as well.
